Automatic Replenishment Consolidation to Trolley

In the current replenishment process, all automatic replenishment Warehouse Tasks are first created to an intermediate Trolley Bin. Subsequently, warehouse users manually create Warehouse Tasks to move stock from the Trolley Bin to the fixed bins in the destination storage location.

To optimize replenishment execution, the system should consolidate automatic replenishment requirements that have the same:

  • Source Location/Bin
  • Material (SKU)
  • Batch
  • Destination Trolley Bin

into a single Warehouse Task with the aggregated quantity.

Expected System Behavior

Instead of creating multiple replenishment Warehouse Tasks to the same trolley, the system shall create one consolidated Warehouse Task when all the above attributes are identical.

Example

Current Scenario

Source Bin

Material

Batch

Destination Trolley

Quantity

A-01-01

MAT001

B123

TR001

10

A-01-01

MAT001

B123

TR001

15

A-01-01

MAT001

B123

TR001

20

Current Result

  • WT1: Qty 10 to TR001
  • WT2: Qty 15 to TR001
  • WT3: Qty 20 to TR001

Proposed Result

  • WT1: Qty 45 to TR001

After the consolidated Warehouse Task is confirmed, warehouse users can continue the existing process of creating replenishment Warehouse Tasks from the Trolley Bin (TR001) to the respective fixed bins in the destination storage location.

entry.title: Replicating WM SU Type-Bin Type Based Empty Bin Determination in EWM
entry.content:
Hello Experts,

Current WM Process

In WM, empty storage bin determination is controlled using a combination of SU Type and Storage Bin Type.

  • During TO creation, users manually enter the SU Type.
  • Physical handling units do not exist 
  • Users select the SU Type based on how the supplier delivers the product (for example, small boxes versus pallets).
  • The system then determines an appropriate empty bin based on the SU Type and bin type relationship.

This approach provides flexibility because the same material may arrive in different load carriers.

 

EWM Challenge

In EWM, during warehouse task creation, we cannot influence storage bin determination by manually selecting an HU Type in the same way.

Current alternatives we are considering is use storage sections and allow users to manually choose the appropriate section (for example, pallet area vs carton area).

entry.title: EWM-to-EWM STO: Residual quantity stuck in Val. GR Blocked Stock (107 posted, missing automatic 109)
entry.content:
We have an STO process between two EWM-managed plants/warehouses.

The outbound delivery contained a total quantity of 16.696 KG for the same material and batch.

During outbound picking, two Handling Units were involved:

  • HU 10032077416 – 8.394 KG
  • HU 10032079519 – 8.302 KG

Both warehouse tasks were successfully confirmed.

However, there is an inconsistency regarding the problematic quantity of 8.302 KG.

For this quantity:

  • Source HU was 10032079519
  • Destination HU in the confirmed Warehouse Task is empty
  • HU 10032079519 is not present in the Handling Units of the final Outbound Delivery

For the successfully processed quantity of 8.394 KG:

  • Source HU = 10032077416
  • Destination HU = 10032077416
  • The HU is correctly present in the Outbound Delivery

    The outbound PGI posted the complete quantity of 16.696 KG with movement type 107.

    On the receiving side, the EWM Inbound Delivery contains only:

    • HU 10032077416
    • Quantity 8.394 KG

    Therefore, only 8.394 KG was processed on the receiving side and automatically posted with movement type 109.

    The remaining 8.302 KG is currently stuck in Valuated GR Blocked Stock.

    The quantity physically exists in the receiving warehouse, but it does not exist as stock in the receiving EWM warehouse.

entry.title: S/4HANA EWM Refurbishment: Exclude Faulty Split Valuation from MRP
entry.content:
Hello Experts,
We are currently optimizing our Repairable Spare Refurbishment Process in SAP S/4HANA (embedded Advanced EWM) and are looking for validation and best practice advice on collapsing our process from two storage locations into one single storage location.
 
Current Setup:
SLoc XXX1 (Functional Stock) & SLoc XXX2 (Defective Stock).S/4HANA
Dismantled serialized spares (IE4N) currently go to the defective storage location as Blocked Stock.
The Issue: Standard SAP design prohibits a Goods Issue via movement type 261 against a PM order out of Blocked stock status. To bypass this restriction and streamline inventory administration, we are looking to eliminate the secondary storage location entirely and manage everything inside a single storage location (SLoc XXX1).
 
Proposed "Single SLoc" Solution using Split Valuation:
We have split valuation configured with two valuation types: Functional and Faulty. Our target design is to:
Return dismantled spares via IE4N directly to the single storage location under the Valuation Type Faulty, but mapped to an ERP status of Unrestricted-Use (allowing us to smoothly execute the 261 GI to the Refurbishment Order).
In Advanced EWM, this ERP Unrestricted/Faulty combination maps to a specific EWM Stock Type (e.g., XX), which we physically isolate via EWM Warehouse Layout Control into a dedicated defective zone/bin area.
 
The MRP Challenge:
Because the defective stock sits logically in an ERP Unrestricted-Use status to allow the consumption movement, the MRP engine naturally counts it as available normal stock, which distorts our net requirements planning.
 
Our Questions to the Community:
 

What is the most robust, standard way to make MRP completely ignore or exclude the Faulty valuation type segment while it resides in an Unrestricted-Use status? Is configuring the MRP Relevancy/Availability Indicator within SPRO > Split Valuation the cleanest route for S/4HANA MRP Live, or are there hidden pitfalls?
Are there any known integration caveats between Advanced EWM Stock Types and ERP Split Valuation when handling PM04 Refurbishment Orders out of a single storage location?
 

Is anyone successfully running this exact single-SLoc architecture for refurbishment, or is a 2-SLoc setup still considered the definitive best practice in S/4HANA + EWM environments?
We would appreciate any insights, configuration tips, or lessons learned from your past projects.
Thank you!

entry.title: Inspection Types for Inspection Lots in SAP EWM
entry.content:
Source of Inspection Types

The key configuration that governs where inspection lot setup data originates is the "Inspection Setup Origin" (I-Lot Setup) field. This is defined per warehouse in the following Customizing path:

SAP Customizing Implementation Guide → SCM Extended Warehouse Management → Extended Warehouse Management → Cross-Process Settings → Quality Management → Basics and Integration → Define and Activate Warehouse-Dependent IOTs

  • Embedded EWM: You have a choice of three options for the Inspection Setup Origin:
    1. No Inspection Rule (available since SAP S/4HANA 1909): Inspection lot setup data is taken directly from the Quality Management tab of the Material Master (transaction MM03). No inspection rule in EWM is required. The standard inspection types supported are 01 (Goods receipt for purchase order), 04 (Goods receipt from production), 08 (Stock transfer inspection), and 09 (Recurring inspection of batches). [1] [2] [3]
    2. From Material Master: Control indicators, inspection types, and other inspection lot setup data are taken from the Inspection Type defined in the Material Master QM view. Note: even in this case, at least one generic inspection rule must still be defined in EWM — otherwise, when posting a GR for a non-quality-inspected material, the system raises error /SCWM/QINSP_S4001. [4] [5]
    3. From Inspection Rule: All inspection lot setup data (control indicators, inspection types, etc.) is taken from the Inspection Rule maintained in transaction /SCWM/QRSETUP. The Material Master QM view settings become redundant in this case. [4] [2]
  • Decentralized EWM: There is no option to choose the Inspection Setup Origin in Customizing. The Inspection Rule (transaction /SCWM/QRSETUP) is always the sole source for inspection lot setup data — including control indicators, inspection types, and all related parameters. Material Master QM view settings for inspection types are not used for inspection lot creation in decentralized EWM. [6] [7] [8]

Control Indicators & Inspection Types

Setting

Embedded EWM

Decentralized EWM

Source of Inspection Type

Material Master QM view (if "No Inspection Rule" or "From Material Master") OR Inspection Rule /SCWM/QRSETUP (if "From Inspection Rule")

Always from Inspection Rule /SCWM/QRSETUP only

Inspection Setup Origin field in Customizing

Available — three options: No Inspection Rule / From Material Master / From Inspection Rule

Not available — Inspection Rule is the only source

Supported Inspection Lot Types (standard)

Without inspection rules: types 01, 04, 08, 09 (lot origin 17 EWM). With inspection rules: custom types also possible via user exit.

Only inspection lot types assigned to lot origin 17 are supported

Inspection Rule required?

Not required since SAP S/4HANA 1909 (when "No Inspection Rule" is selected); still required for "From Material Master" (at least one generic rule) and "From Inspection Rule"

Always required

Quality Inspection Engine (QIE)

Not used — QM is called directly within the same S/4HANA stack

Required — QIE acts as the integration layer between EWM and S/4HANA QM

Supported IOTs

IOT 3, IOT 4, IOT 5, IOT 7

All IOTs (IOT 1 available up to EWM 9.5)

Custom Inspection Types

Possible via user exit EXIT_SAPLQPL1_005 (implement SAP Notes (https://me.sap.com/notes/3508507) and (https://me.sap.com/notes/3487253)) when "No Inspection Rule" is used

Specify custom type in inspection rule; must be assigned to lot origin 17 in QM Customizing

[2] [9] [7] [10] [6] [11]

SAP's Recommendation

SAP recommends maintaining the "From Material Master" origin when: [4] [5]

  • You operate both Embedded EWM and Decentralized EWM for the same plant and want to use the same inspection type settings across both instances.

SAP recommends maintaining the "From Inspection Rule" origin when: [4]

  • You run SAP S/4HANA Embedded EWM only with no plans to connect another EWM system, and you want a single, centralized place to maintain inspection lot setup data — including the ability to group multiple materials via quality inspection groups.

Key Configuration Path

  1. Define Inspection Setup Origin per Warehouse (Embedded EWM): SAP Customizing Implementation Guide → SCM Extended Warehouse Management → Extended Warehouse Management → Cross-Process Settings → Quality Management → Basics and Integration → Define and Activate Warehouse-Dependent IOTs Select the warehouse + IOT combination → double-click to open the form view → set Insp. Setup Origin. [10] [2]
  2. Maintain Inspection Rules (Decentralized EWM & Embedded EWM when rules are used): Transaction /SCWM/QRSETUP — define the inspection type (must be assigned to lot origin 17 in QM Customizing), properties (material, quality inspection group, supplier), inspection scope (sample or 100%), decision codes, findings, and follow-up actions. [12] [7] [9]
  3. Maintain Inspection Types in QM Customizing (Decentralized EWM prerequisite): Quality Management → Quality Inspection → Inspection Lot Creation → Maintain Inspection Types AND Quality Management → Quality Inspection → Inspection Lot Creation → Maintain Inspection Lot Origins and Assign Inspection Types → Ensure the inspection type is assigned to lot origin 17. [7] [8]
  4. Maintain Material Master QM View (Embedded EWM — "No Inspection Rule" or "From Material Master"): Transaction MM03 → Quality Management tab → set the relevant inspection type (e.g., 01, 04, 08, 09). [1] [3]

entry.title: SAP EWM–ERP Serial Number Mismatch During Delivery Processing
entry.content:
Hi SAP Community,

We are facing an issue where the serial number format differs between EWM and ERP.

For example:

  • EWM: 01-02-2345

  • ERP: 2345-2-1

When the delivery is processed, the serial number sent from EWM does not match the one in ERP, causing the queue to get stuck due to a serial number mismatch.

We also found that many serial numbers were uploaded incorrectly during the initial stock upload, which has resulted in further mismatches.

Has anyone faced a similar issue? Is there a standard configuration, mapping, or BAdI available to handle this serial number format conversion between EWM and ERP?

Any suggestions would be appreciated. Thanks!

entry.title: Skip POSC for HUs Containing a Single Product
entry.content:
Requirement: Skip POSC for HUs Containing a Single Product

Our requirement is to bypass the POSC process and proceed directly to putaway when an HU contains a single product. If the HU contains multiple products, the POSC process should be triggered.

One possible workaround is to use different document types, item types, and WPTs. However, the client expects to achieve this using the same WPT for both scenarios.

Is there any standard configuration or enhancement available to determine whether POSC should be triggered based on the number of products in the HU, without maintaining separate WPTs?

Any suggestions or guidance on how to achieve this would be appreciated.
